_meta.description: Updated Stage 3 (Credentialized) for the universal Anaplan product Delivery journey template. Slots into the larger template at stages[2]. Reflects iteration from Stage 3 review pass.
changes_from_previous: Removed: Configuration Guide reading task (moved to Stage 2 as reference material with guided walkthrough)
Removed: Integration Architecture Patterns reading task (moved to Anaplan Platform prereq journey)
Removed: Pre-delivery readiness check-in with PSM (no longer needed; the workshop completion + Top-10-Extensions course are the Stage 3 → Stage 4 gate)
Consolidated: Sandbox model build + Deep-Dive Enablement + Regional Implementer Workshop into a single Delivery Readiness Workshop construct (these were three names for the same hands-on activity)

Restructured: Stage 3 hands-on work expressed as a week-long cohort-based workshop — three 2-hour instructor-led sessions (Monday, Wednesday, Friday) with three ~1-hour labs completed by the participant between and after sessions
Added: New completion mechanism `lab_verification` for tooling-verified lab outcomes
Added: Stage entry verification gate `tenant-access-active` (verifies the auto-provisioning that fired in Stage 2 succeeded)
Changed: Top-10-Extensions content is mandatory and authored as an Academy course (academy_xls verification), placed after the workshop concludes
Decision: Phase remains `learning` — even though Stage 3 is hands-on, the customer is not in the loop and the participant is still being taught. Stage 4 is the first true `doing` stage.
Decision: Sessions are sequential within a cohort — participants register for the cohort and attend Mon/Wed/Fri as a group
Decision: Labs are tooling-verified pass/fail, no scoring
Decision: Lab dependencies are lab-chain (Lab N requires Lab N-1 passed) — labs build on each other in the sandbox
open_items_parked_for_later: Lab failure handling — what the participant sees on lab failure (just 'try again' vs. hints/diagnostics) and whether there is an automatic escalation path after repeated failures. Operational policy, not structural.
Missed-session policy — default for v0 is 'reschedule into next cohort', but recordings, makeup sessions, or individual catch-up are alternatives worth revisiting.
Cohort cadence — how often regional cohorts run. Affects how long a participant waits between Stage 2 completion and Stage 3 entry.
Per-lab effort estimates within the ~1-hour bound — to be refined once labs are authored per product.
Lab tooling integration spec — how the verification tooling reports lab outcomes back to the journey system.
Per-product Top-10-Extensions Academy course — must be authored per product.
_meta.boundary_with_stage_4: End of Stage 3: participant has demonstrated configuration-side competency in a controlled sandbox via instructor-led workshop with tooling-verified labs, and has been exposed to the field's most common extensions for {{PRODUCT_NAME}}. They have NOT touched a real customer engagement. Stage 4 covers tasks leading up to and through real client deployments. Verb shift: hands-on with sandbox → hands-on with customer.

_note: Stage 3 task structure is FIXED across all product journeys. Workshop session content and lab content are VARIABLE per product — sessions and labs map to the same six configuration-side methodology phases (phases 5-10 from Stage 2 Block C), but the session material, sandbox data, customer scenarios, and pass criteria are product-specific.
name: Credentialized
description: Participant demonstrates configuration-side competency by completing the Delivery Readiness Workshop — a week-long cohort-based experience with three 2-hour instructor-led sessions (Monday, Wednesday, Friday) and three ~1-hour tooling-verified labs completed between and after sessions. Closes with the Top-10-Extensions Academy course covering the most common field patterns for {{PRODUCT_NAME}}.

tasks._fixed: task definition fixed; session and lab content variable per product
tasks._note: Single workshop task containing six sub-units (3 sessions + 3 labs) interleaved across a week. Sessions are instructor-led and cohort-based (Mon/Wed/Fri). Labs are self-paced and tooling-verified, completed between/after sessions. Replaces what was historically called Implementer Workshop, Deep-Dive Enablement, and Sandbox Model Build.
tasks.title: {{PRODUCT_NAME}} Delivery Readiness Workshop
tasks.description: Week-long cohort-based workshop covering configuration-side methodology phases 5-10. Three 2-hour instructor-led sessions delivered Monday, Wednesday, and Friday, paired with three ~1-hour labs completed by the participant between and after sessions. Each session teaches content; each lab applies it in the provisioned sandbox with tooling-verified pass/fail.
tasks.estimated_effort: 9 hrs total (6 hrs instructor-led + 3 hrs labs), spread over ~1 week elapsed
tasks._completion_mechanism_note: Workshop is complete when all 3 sessions are admin_signoff confirmed AND all 3 labs are lab_verification passed.

sub_units.title: Session 1 — Customer Data Validation & Application Configuration

sub_units.schedule: Between Mon and Wed (participant's own time)
sub_units.title: Lab 1 — Customer data validation + configuration practice

sub_units.schedule: Between Wed and Fri (participant's own time)
sub_units.title: Lab 2 — Loading and validation practice

tasks._lab_failure_handling_status: TBD — operational policy. Default for v0: simple retry, no escalation. Adjustable post-launch.
tasks._missed_session_handling_status: TBD — operational policy. Default for v0: reschedule into next cohort. Recordings, makeup sessions, or individual catch-up are alternatives worth revisiting.

tasks._fixed: task definition fixed; course content variable per product
tasks.title: {{PRODUCT_NAME}} Top 10 Extensions Academy course
tasks.description: Mandatory Academy course authored by the {{PRODUCT_NAME}} CoE / product team covering the 10 extensions most commonly seen in the field for {{PRODUCT_NAME}}. Field-experience content the participant cannot get from a lab — Lab 3 teaches the mechanics of building extensions; this course teaches what extensions to expect and how to approach them in real customer engagements. Includes a completion quiz.
tasks._placement_note: Required to be completed AFTER the Delivery Readiness Workshop (workshop completion unlocks the course).

stage_entry_gates.description: {{PRODUCT_NAME}} delivery workspaces and workshop models provisioned and accessible (verifies the auto-provisioning action that fired in Stage 2 succeeded)

_stage_entry_gates_note: Stage 3 has a stage-entry verification gate (tenant access) separate from the per-task gates. This is a verification-only check — provisioning was triggered in Stage 2; Stage 3 just confirms it landed.

gates.description: {{PRODUCT_NAME}} Top 10 Extensions Academy course completion confirmed (quiz passed)

_estimated_effort_total_note: Computed from 6 hrs instructor-led + 3 hrs labs + 45-60 min extensions course. Spread over ~1 week elapsed (Mon/Wed/Fri sessions plus interleaved lab time plus post-workshop course).

_per_product_authoring_obligations.description: For every product journey instantiation, the following must be authored. The template specifies; the product team produces.

assets.note: Sessions cover methodology phases 5-10, paired 2 phases per session.
Each lab requires sandbox data, scenario, and pass criteria definition. Labs build on each other in the sandbox.
Content scope: the 10 extensions most commonly seen in the field for this product.

infrastructure.scope: List of workspaces and models constituting the Stage 3 workshop environment for {{PRODUCT_NAME}}. Triggered in Stage 2; verified at Stage 3 entry.
Lab verification tooling must be configured per product to accept lab submissions, run pass/fail checks, and report outcomes back to the journey system.
Regional cohort cadence and registration mechanism. Defines when participants can enter Stage 3.
